about: Which checks a change needs, written once. scripts/classify-ci-changes.js reads this file to decide which CI jobs run, and tests keep the audio workflow's paths equal to it.

A path is looked up in the rules in order, and the first rule that matches decides its checks. A change needs the checks of every path it touches, a removed or renamed file's old path included. A path no rule matches gets every check CI decides, and a test fails until a rule names it.
A pattern is a path, a folder followed by /** for everything in it, or a path with * for part of one name and **/ for any folders. Nothing else is read.
CI decides from the base commit's copy of this file and of the classifier, so a pull request can't choose its own checks.

repo.about: Lint, the unit tests and Firefox's lint of the build. Every change needs it.

extension.about: The real extension in Chromium and in the installed Firefox.

ui.about: The popup's layout in each state and the limiter stage, in Chromium and in Firefox's engine.

site.about: The website and its demo, which the same command checks.

audio-hosted.about: Both jobs of the Audio suites workflow on the pull request's final commit, none skipped or cancelled. GitHub starts it from the workflow's own paths, and it isn't a required check, so look at it by hand.

audio-mac.about: The audio suites on this Mac, on the pull request's final commit. Firefox plays the tone aloud, so ask first.

listen.when: the change can affect how the effect sounds
listen.about: Listen to reverb, echo, EQ, width and saturation with music.

firefox-frame-look.when: the popup's frame changed in CSS
firefox-frame-look.about: Look at the real popup in Firefox, with its rounded panel corners.

permission-steps.when: the permission code changed: the manifest's permissions, or how the extension asks for access or handles it
permission-steps.about: The permission and revoking steps of RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md, in each browser.

site-popup-sync.about: Copy the popup into the website. The tests fail while the copy is out of date.

rules.about: The audio workflow, which is also one of the workflows below.
What decides and enforces which checks run: the workflows (Dependabot's action updates included), the classifier and this map. A change to them runs every check CI decides.
Documentation, wherever it is, the store text and the privacy policy included. A change only to the audio suite's documentation needs none of its runs.
Repository settings, the unit tests, the store's files, and the tools that render or release, which no browser test runs.
The audio engines. The limiter stage in them is part of what the popup and limiter tests render.
The background script and the content scripts.
The settings: defaults, ranges and presets. The background script, the content script and the popup load them, and the website has a copy.
The manifest, which decides what is injected where and which access the extension may ask for.
The popup's page and script. The audio suites never open the popup, so they don't run for it; what it sends to the tab, and how often, can still change the sound.
The popup's styles.
The icons, which scripts/render-icons.js makes. They are pictures: a script put among them has no rule.
The audio suite. CI runs every browser test for it too, as it did before this map, though nothing shows they use it.
What the audio suites share with the extension's browser tests: the disposable copy of the build and starting Firefox.
What every local test server reads its request targets with, the audio suites' included.
Dependencies, the Node.js version, and what the CI jobs install their packages and Firefox with. They can change any test's result.
The extension's browser tests.
The build of the store packages, which the extension's browser tests and the audio suites load. It adds Firefox's permissions.
What measures the popup for both the extension's browser test and the popup's layout tests.
The popup, limiter and website tests, and what serves the popup and the website to them.
The website's demo, which has its own copy of the limiter stage.
The website.
Not sorted yet. Nothing shows the browser tests use these, but CI ran them for these before this map, as for any path it didn't know, and still does.
